column2: The observer of the Shat-tila-dvadashi vow attains heaven with good merit; the Manoratha-dvadashi doer should worship in the bright half of Phalguna.
One who keeps the Nama-dvadashi vow should worship Hari for a year with the names beginning with Keshava; a man so doing is not a denizen of hell but one of heaven.
Having worshipped in the bright half of Phalguna, the Sumati-dvadashi vower; in the bright month of Bhadrapada, the Ananta-dvadashi vower;
under Ashlesha or Mula, or in Magha, "homage to Krishna": one should worship, and the Tila-dvadashi man should offer sesame in the fire.
The Sugati-dvadashi doer should worship in the bright half of Phalguna: "Victory, Krishna, homage to you"; for a year he becomes a sharer of enjoyment and liberation.
On the twelfth of the bright half of Pausha, the vower of the Sampti-dvadashi.
Vishnu bearing umbrella and staff: "Homage, homage to Vamana. I give arghya, lord of gods, ever worshipped with the arghya-worthy and the rest;
make me endowed with enjoyment, liberation, offspring, fame and all lordship." "Homage to Vamana" — the incense; with this the oblation, a hundred and eight times.
Om homage to Vasudeva — one should worship Hari's head; to Shridhara the face likewise; to Krishna the throat;
homage to Shripati the chest; to the bearer of all weapons the arms; "homage to the all-pervading" the navel; "homage to Vamana" the waist;
to the conqueror of the three worlds the generative organ; the shanks of Hari one should worship; "to the lord of all" the feet; "to Vishnu, the Self of all."
One should give ghee-cooked food offering and pots with curd rice. Having kept vigil at night, in the morning, having bathed at the confluence,
having worshipped with scents and flowers, one should say this with a handful of flowers: "Homage, homage to you, Govinda, known to the wise by hearing;
having destroyed the flood of sin, be giver of all happiness. May you be pleased, god, lord of gods, Janardana, always with me.
Vamana is the giver of intellect, the giver, abiding in wealth; Vamana himself receives; Vamana gives to me;
Vamana ever abides in wealth; homage, homage to Vamana." Having given the fee, having fed Brahmins, one should eat oneself.

Whatever vow of mine in seven births was broken, O Lord, by your grace let it be unbroken here.
agnipuran:190:4	As this whole world is unbroken in you alone, Purushottama, so may all my vows be unbroken.
So also monthly the Chaturmasya rule is remembered. Besides, in the months from Chaitra one should offer vessels of barley meal;
beginning from Shravana and ending in Kartika, the breaking of the fast; the defects of vows in seven births are made fruitful.
One obtains long life, health, good fortune, kingdom, enjoyment and the rest.
Having tasted kakola water, the vower should worship in Phalguna; having eaten camphor, in Chaitra he becomes fortunate in his form;
in Vaishakha one should worship Mahariipa, eating nutmeg; in Jyeshtha eating cloves the vower should worship Pradyumna;
in Ashadha eating sesame-water one should worship Uma's husband; in Shravana eating scented water one should worship the trident-bearer;
in Bhadrapada having tasted, one should worship Sadyojata, the teacher; in Ashvina having drunk golden water, the lord of the thirty gods;
in Kartika Vishveshvara; eating madana fruit the vower should worship; at the end of the year Shiva of the winter, covered with a mango leaf,
having worshipped with cloth, one should give to a Brahmin a cow, and a bed, umbrella, pots, sandals, vessel of juices.
On the thirteenth of the bright half of Chaitra, remembering Rati and Priti, having drawn a tree called Ashoka with vermilion and turmeric,
one should worship for a year, desiring desire — the Kama-trayodashi vow.
On the fourteenth and the eighth in both bright and dark fortnights, fasting, one should worship Shambhu; one gets heaven — the both-fourteenth vow;
by night-meal on the dark eighth and likewise the dark fourteenth, one gets enjoyments here and a good state hereafter.
On the dark fourteenth of Kartika the bather is happy; when Mahendra is worshipped, on poles shaped as banners;
then on the bright fourteenth one should worship Ananta Hari, having made a figure of darbha with a water-vessel,
of a prastha of rice flour, made into cakes; half should be given to the Brahmin, half one should join to oneself;
at the river's end, having told Hari's tale: "In the great ocean of endless samsara, lift up the sunk, Vasudeva;
engage us in the infinite form; homage, homage to you of infinite form." Having worshipped with this, and having tied a consecrated thread
on one's own hand or throat, the doer of the Ananta vow is happy.
On the fifteenth of Magha, having worshipped the Unborn, one obtains everything. I shall tell the Savitri new-moon, auspicious, giving enjoyment and liberation:
on the fifteenth in Jyeshtha at the root of a banyan, a woman who has fasted three nights should worship the great faithful Savitri with seven grains,
with sprouted ones, neck-threads, and at night with saffron and the like; having hung on the banyan, with dance and song at dawn,
Homage to Savitri, to Satyavan — one should offer food to a Brahmin; having gone home and fed Brahmins, having eaten herself, she should dismiss them:
May the goddess Savitri be pleased; she obtains good fortune and the rest.
Having taken up on Sunday at Hasta the night-meal for a year, he is a sharer in all; having done seven Mondays at Chitra he becomes happy;
having taken Mars at Svati, seven night-meals free him of affliction; having taken Mercury at Vishakha, seven night-meals destroy planetary affliction;
at Anuradha, the gods' teacher; seven night-meals destroy planetary affliction; having taken Venus at Jyeshtha, seven night-meals destroy planetary affliction;
having taken Saturn at Mula, seven night-meals destroy planetary affliction.
Vishnu as the Nakshatra-Purusha, Shiva-formed, is to be worshipped. The vower of the Shambhavayaniya vow should worship Hari in the month's star;
in Kartika at Krittika, in Margashirsha at Mrigashiras, with the names beginning with Keshava, or with "homage to Achyuta":

In Kartika, on the day of Krittika, I shall perform the Shambhavayaniya vow of Hari in the month's star, giver of enjoyment and liberation;
agnipuran:196:11	the great form beginning with Keshava, Achyuta, giver of all, I invoke, the god who increases life and health.
From Kartika for four months, food with sakasara; from Phalguna, kushara; from Ashadha, pudding;
to the god and to Brahmins one should offer the night-meal food; bathed in pancha-gavya water, by partaking of that alone he is pure.
All material before dismissal is called the offering; when the Lord of the world is dismissed it becomes remnant in a moment.

Homage, homage to you, Achyuta; may my sin perish, may merit increase; may my lordship, wealth and the rest be ever imperishable, and may my line not perish.
agnipuran:196:16	As you, Achyuta, are beyond the beyond, that Brahman-become, beyond, O supreme Self, so make Achyuta my desire; remover of sin done by me, immeasurable.
Achyuta, Ananda, Govinda, be pleased with what I desire; make me imperishable, immeasurable Self, Purushottama.
Having worshipped for seven years one obtains enjoyment and liberation. I shall tell the Ananta vow, yielding wealth among the star-vows:
in Margashirsha at Mrigashiras, eating cow-urine, one should worship Hari; Ananta, the Lord, is the fruit of all desires;
he gives the infinite, and that same elsewhere in another birth; this great vow produces infinite accumulation of merit;
it brings attainment of one's wish and imperishability. Having worshipped from the feet and so on, one should eat at night without oil;
oblation with ghee directed to Ananta for four months; from Chaitra oblation with rice; from Shravana with milk.
Mandhata, son of Yuvanashva, was born through the Ananta vow.
One who would perform the three-night vow addressed to Janardana, taking a hundred families, goes to Hari's abode.
On the ninth in the bright half of Margashirsha the vower should begin the three-night vow by rule;
one should repeat "Om homage to Vasudeva" a thousand or a hundred times; on the eighth eating one meal, he should fast three days;
on the twelfth he should worship Vishnu; in Kartika one should have the vow done. Having fed Brahmins, garments, beds and seats,
umbrella, sacred thread, vessels one should give, and request the twice-born: "In this hard vow whatever of mine was deficient,
by your permission let that be complete." Having enjoyed enjoyments the doer of the three-night vow goes to Vishnu.
I shall tell the Kartika vow, giving enjoyment and liberation: on the tenth eating pancha-gavya, fasting on the eleventh,
having worshipped Vishnu in the bright half of Kartika, he goes in a divine aerial car. In Chaitra, a night-eater three nights, giver of five goats, is happy.
Three nights drinking milk, three days fasting devoted, from the sixth in the bright Kartika, the Krichchhra is called Mahendra;
five nights drinking milk, living on curds, fasting, on the eleventh in Kartika — this Krichchhra is the Bhaskara, yielding wealth.
Barley gruel, yavaka, vegetable, curds, milk, ghee, water — from the fifth in the bright half; the Krichchhra is remembered as Shantapana.
For the four months from Shravana the vower obtains everything by vows. In the bright half of Ashadha, having fasted on the eleventh,
one should make the arrangement of the Chaturmasya vows. On Ashadhi, or at the sun's entry into Cancer, one should worship Hari;
This vow has been taken by me, god, before you; may it reach unobstructed success, you being pleased, Keshava.
